merger_description:
Pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement, Dicker Data Limited (**Dicker Data**) proposes to acquire all 2,196,009 fully paid ordinary shares in Sektor Group Limited (**Sektor**). As a result of this transfer, Dicker Data will indirectly acquire an interest in Sektor Limited, Sektor Pty Ltd and Sektor LP Pty Ltd, Sektor Distributors SDN BHD and Sektor (Thailand) Co. Ltd which are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Sektor.

Dicker Data is an ASX-listed company distributing a broad range of IT and IT-related products and value-added services to resellers in Australia and New Zealand, including the supply of networking hardware and software solutions enabling devices and cybersecurity hardware and software solutions.

Sektor and its subsidiaries also distribute IT and IT-related products and value-added services to resellers in Australia, New Zealand, Thailand and Malaysia, focussing on Point of Sale (**POS**), Enterprise Mobility and Automatic Identification and Data Capture (**AIDC**), Cybersecurity and Networking.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between the types of IT
and IT-related products the parties distribute in Australia,
as the majority of Sektor’s revenue is generated from the
distribution of product segments which Dicker Data does
not provide
b. the increment in share in the wholesale IT and IT-related
products, and networking and cybersecurity products,
arising from the Acquisition is expected to be low
c. there are alternative wholesale providers of IT and IT-
related products, and cybersecurity and networking
products, in Australia and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
